name: labor-market
description: A labor market with no minimum wage. Firms of one sector compete for workers whose capacity grows with work; workers want higher pay but must cover the cost of living to survive. Firms make individual offers based on a noisy read of each candidate, poach each other's workers, and counter outside offers. A minimum wage exists only as a yardstick to classify people into poverty, lower, middle and upper class.

minimumWage.description: Reference minimum wage per month. Used only to classify income; it does not bind any wage

subsistence.description: Cost of living per month: basic food and housing

monthsShortToDie.description: Consecutive months unable to pay the cost of living that kill a person

basePrice.description: Price of one unit of output when the sector produces baseDemand units a month

baseDemand.description: Units a month the market buys at basePrice

elasticity.description: Price elasticity of demand: price = basePrice x (output / baseDemand)^(-1/elasticity)

fixedCost.description: Monthly overhead of a firm (rent, systems), paid to suppliers outside the model

startingCapital.description: Cash a new firm starts with, put in by owners outside the model

cashBufferMonths.description: Months of payroll and overhead a firm wants in cash before it hires

payoutAboveMonths.description: Profit is paid out to the owners as dividends as long as this many months of costs stay in the bank

hireRate.description: Most a firm can grow in a month, as a share of its headcount (recruiting capacity)

minHires.description: Openings a firm can recruit for in a month, however small it is

interviewsPerOpening.description: Job seekers a firm interviews per opening

interviewNoise.description: Standard deviation of the relative error of an interview's read of a candidate's capacity

hiringCost.description: Cost of a hire (recruiting, onboarding), in months of the wage offered

markdownRise.description: How much a firm lowers its offers (raises the markdown) after a month in which it filled all its openings

markdownCut.description: How much a firm raises its offers after a month with openings left unfilled, x the share unfilled

expectedTenure.description: Months a firm expects a new hire to stay, used to weigh what a hire earns against what it costs

layoffTolerance.description: How far below their wage a person's value may fall before the firm considers a layoff (labor hoarding)

counterMargin.description: Least share of a worker's value the current employer keeps when matching an outside offer

switchPremium.description: Raise an employed worker requires to move to another firm

reservationDecay.description: Monthly drop of an unemployed person's lowest acceptable wage

offerLearning.description: Share of the distance between the wage a job seeker expects and the best offer it got that it revises each month

runwayComfort.description: Months of savings above which an unemployed person is not pressed to lower the wage it asks

searchBase.description: Monthly chance that an employed person looks for another job while paid like its peers

searchGap.description: Extra weight of looking for another job per unit of pay shortfall against the peers' average wage

mpcLow.description: Share of the wage above subsistence that people with low pay spend

mpcHigh.description: Share of the wage above subsistence that people with very high pay spend

wealthSpending.description: Share of savings spent each month (about 5% a year): consumption out of wealth

learningRate.description: Monthly share of the distance to one's talent closed by working

skillDecay.description: Monthly share of capacity lost while unemployed

plenoCapacity.description: Capacity at which an employer promotes a junior to pleno

seniorCapacity.description: Capacity at which an employer promotes a pleno to senior

entrantsPerMonth.description: Young people entering the labor market each month, on average

entrantSavingsMonths.description: Entrants bring from their family up to this many months of living costs (drawn uniformly from 0)

entryAge.description: Age at which people enter the labor market, in months (18 years)

retirementAge.description: Age at which people retire and leave the labor market, in months (65 years)

mortalityBase.description: Gompertz a: yearly chance of dying of natural causes at age 0

mortalityGrowth.description: Gompertz b: growth of the yearly risk per year of age

entrySensitivity.description: Monthly chance that a new firm enters, per unit of the sector's profit margin

maxEntryChance.description: Highest monthly chance that a new firm enters

initialEmployment.description: Share of people employed at the start

price.description: Price of a unit of output this month

output.description: Units produced by the sector this month

meanWage.description: Average wage of the employed this month

levelWage.description: Average wage by level (junior, pleno, senior): what salary surveys publish

profitMargin.description: Profit of the sector over its revenue last month

hhi.description: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of output shares (0 to 1)

seeking.description: This month's job seekers, by agent id: the lowest wage each accepts. Only the market reads it

jobChanges.description: Employed people who moved to another firm this month

counteroffers.description: Outside offers matched by the current employer this month

layoffs.description: People laid off this month, including by bankruptcy

bankruptcies.description: Firms that went bankrupt this month

deaths.description: People who died this month for lack of income

naturalDeaths.description: People who died this month of natural causes

unemployment.description: Share of the labor force without a job

poverty.description: Share of the labor force earning less than 1 minimum wage (unemployed included)

upperClass.description: Share earning more than 10 minimum wages

seniors.description: Share of the labor force at the senior level

worker.description: A person in the labor market. Must pay the cost of living every month; wants the highest pay it can get; knows its level and experience, not its exact capacity.

capacity.description: Output per month. Grows with work toward talent, decays while unemployed. Only the employer observes it

talent.description: Capacity a lifetime of work approaches

expectedWage.description: What the person believes it can earn: the wage of its job, or for the unemployed the last wage revised toward the offers received

bestOffer.description: Best offer received last month while unemployed; 0 when none

employer.description: Id of the employing firm; 0 when unemployed

monthsUnemployed.description: Months in a row without a job

monthsShort.description: Months in a row unable to pay the cost of living

experience.description: Months worked in total (shown on the CV)

level.description: Title given by employers; never goes down

firm.description: A firm of the sector. Wants to grow its profit by employing capable workers; knows the true capacity of its own staff and reads candidates through interviews.

cash.description: Money in the bank; below what the payroll needs, the firm goes bankrupt

markdown.description: Share of a candidate's estimated value the firm tries to keep when making an offer

openings.description: Jobs the firm is recruiting for this month

layoffsPlanned.description: People the firm decided to lay off this month

capacitySum.description: Total capacity of the staff: output per month

underwater.description: Staff whose value to the firm is more than layoffTolerance below their wage

search.description: Look for a job: the unemployed almost always, the employed more often the more they earn below their level's average wage. Registers the lowest wage the person accepts.

expand.description: Open jobs when a hire is expected to earn the firm more than it costs to recruit (markdown over the expected tenure against the hiring cost) and the firm has a cash cushion; less eagerly while it is losing money.
expand.propensity: 5 * sigmoid(-1 + markdown * ctx.expectedTenure - ctx.hiringCost * (1 - markdown) + 5 * margin)

downsize.description: Lay off staff who are clearly worth less to the firm than they cost.

rules.name: setup
rules.description: Starting jobs: a share of people already work at a random firm, paid what that firm would offer them

rules.name: new_month
rules.description: Resets monthly counters and last month's job seekers

rules.name: entrants
rules.description: Young people enter the labor market

rules.name: production
rules.description: Firms produce and sell at the market price, pay wages, overhead and dividends; firms that cannot pay go bankrupt. Publishes the price, wages by level and each firm's books

rules.name: living
rules.description: People pay the cost of living and spend part of the rest; skills grow or decay; ageing, retirement and death

rules.name: layoffs
rules.description: Firms that decided to downsize lay off the staff with the lowest value for their wage

rules.name: labor_market
rules.description: Firms interview job seekers and make offers; people take the best one; employers may match offers made to their staff

rules.name: promotions
rules.description: Yearly review: employers promote staff whose capacity reached the next level

rules.name: firm_entry
rules.description: New firms enter while the sector is profitable

rules.name: census
rules.description: Unemployment and the income classes measured in minimum wages
